results.title: Netherlands vs Sweden predictions for the 2026 World Cup | Historical Soccer
highlights:
Betfair prices Netherlands at 5/8 to win, the draw at 29/10 and Sweden at 4/1. Converting those to implied probability, the market assigns roughly 62% chance of a Dutch win, 26% to the draw, and approximately 20% to Sweden taking all three points. Those figures align closely with what Polymarket traders are saying. In the Group F winner market, Netherlands are priced at 54 cents, representing a 54% chance of topping the group entirely. Sweden sit well back at single figures, which reflects the gap in squad depth rather than any disrespect for what Potter's side achieved in qualifying.
[...]
Polymarket's real-time data is worth noting for what it implies beyond this specific fixture. Netherlands are considered one of the more realistic semi-final contenders at this tournament, with the Group F draw seen as favourable. Sweden's odds to advance from the group are respectable but not comfortable. The market is not pricing in a Swedish upset here, and the historical head-to-head record, where Netherlands have won three of the last five competitive meetings, supports that position.
[...]
Sweden's path to an upset is narrow but it exists. It runs almost entirely through Viktor Gyokeres. If he is sharp and finds space against Timber and Van Dijk, he is the kind of striker who converts single moments into results. Potter's 3-4-2-1 system is designed to absorb pressure and transition quickly, and Sweden have shown in the play-offs that they can compete in tight, high-pressure matches when the occasion demands it. The problem is that World Cup group games at this level are not quite the same as play-off semifinals, and Sweden will need more than Gyokeres alone to find a win.
[...]
The most likely outcome is a Netherlands victory by a single goal, probably decided by a moment of quality from Gakpo or Reijnders in the second half. Sweden will stay compact and competitive for long stretches, and Gyokeres will cause problems. The Dutch are unlikely to run away with this one. But their composure in decisive moments, a quality built over decades of tournament football, gives them the edge when the margin is thin.
[...]
A draw is the result Sweden should target as a realistic floor. If they arrive in Houston with a win over Tunisia from the opener, a point against Netherlands keeps progression firmly in their own hands for the final game against Japan. That scenario, two European sides both needing something from the fixture, is where tournament football tends to produce its most compelling ninety minutes.

# Preview: Australia vs Turkey - prediction, team news, lineups | 2026 World Cup
[...]
BC Place will play host to an intriguing 2026 World Cup fixture on Saturday, as Australia tackle Turkey in Group D.
[...]
## Match preview
[...]
Australia have been present in each of the last five World Cups, so it is not a surprise that they managed to secure qualification for the 2026 competition, and the national team actually reached the round of 16 in the 2022 tournament - their joint-best showing at this level.
[...]
It will be difficult for the Socceroos to make a serious impression at this summer's tournament, but they will be expecting to get out of a group which also includes USA and Paraguay.
[...]
Turkey, meanwhile, are playing in the World Cup for just the third time, and it is their first appearance since 2002, when they reached the semi-finals and ultimately finished third.
[...]
The Crescent-Stars made the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and boast some serious talent, so they are a team to be taken seriously at this summer's tournament, especially considering their recent form, putting together an eight-game unbeaten run.
[...]
Vincenzo Montella's side have been victorious in seven of their last eight matches, including their two pre-World Cup friendlies, beating North Macedonia 4-0 and Venezuela 2-1.
[...]
Turkey, who have proven that they are capable of advancing deep into a World Cup, beat Kosovo 1-0 in the European playoff final back in March to secure their spot at the tournament.
